text:
Evidence supports concern about rare-edge noise, but I found no direct comparison covering all requested methods on the four specified Amazon categories. [Dunning (1993)](https://aclanthology.org/J93-1003/) shows that count-based mutual-information estimates can overestimate association at small counts. Positive clipping does not address that estimation problem. A lexical-association comparison, [Improving a Fundamental Measure of Lexical Association](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4063q17v), found count-discounted PMI and context-distribution smoothing among the most consistently effective corrections across eight tasks; this is supporting evidence from language, not sequential-recommendation validation.

Sparse Amazon histories make the concern plausible: [SASRec](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/icdm18.pdf) identifies Beauty/Games as particularly sparse, without establishing results for these four categories. Distinct-user edge support measures replication across users; raw transition counts can include repeated evidence from one user. Minimum-support filtering removes weakly supported edges, while shrinkage such as c/(c+λ) attenuates them continuously. These are proposed safeguards, not demonstrated winners here. Source-level reliability alone cannot establish reliability of every outgoing edge. Also, [Don’t Recommend the Obvious](https://www.amazon.science/publications/dont-recommend-the-obvious-estimate-probability-ratios) connects PMI gains specifically to popularity-sampled evaluation; transfer to the pinned candidate protocol needs validation.

An appropriate ungated control is SASRec plus one transition scorer with a fixed, validation-tuned global mixture weight. Hold history windows, recency weights, normalization, candidates and tuning budget constant; compare conditional transition probability, positive log-lift, smoothed log-lift, then independently add edge-count shrinkage, distinct-user shrinkage and minimum-support filtering. Separately cross each scorer with fixed versus adaptive multiple-source gating. Include SASRec alone and transition-only results; report category HR@10, macro-average, edge coverage and performance by support bucket. This separates scoring improvements from gating effects.
